sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the scoreboards
sections.what: Brings in the weekly figures function, the weekly figure type and the data access module.
sections.why: Likely reason: the file gathers its numbers from other modules instead of querying the database directly.

sections.name: Scoreboards
sections.title: Shape of the scoreboards
sections.what: Defines the four groups of fields the dashboard receives, including the freshness list and the model cost figures.
sections.why: A fixed shape keeps the builder and the dashboard page agreeing on field names.
sections.watch_out: Renaming a field here means the dashboard page must change too.

sections.name: buildScoreboards
sections.title: Builds all scoreboard numbers
sections.what: Collects a week of data, then works out freshness per source, the share of model answers that passed the check, the average model cost per priced call, and how many users exist. Missing figures become empty text or null rather than zero.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the file's own comment about honest no-data states.
sections.watch_out: The model cost is an average over priced calls only, while the read count includes all calls, so the two numbers do not describe the same set.

summary: Builds the admin-only dashboard data with four groups of measures: trust, product, learning and business.
purpose: Gives the owner one view of data freshness, model checks, usage and cost, and states honestly when a figure does not exist yet.
why: The file comment says it shows honest no-data messages instead of zeros, so missing figures become text or null.
how: Fetches the last seven days of data in parallel, counts or sums it, then assembles the four groups into one object with a timestamp. Several fields are fixed text saying the metric is not collected yet.
inputs: The current time, plus data read through the repo module and the weekly figures from the analytics module.
outputs: A Scoreboards object with generatedAt and the four groups.
risks: Several business and learning values are fixed text, so they can look like measured results. The model cost value is an average per priced call, not a total.
debug: If a number looks wrong, check the repo queries it calls and the verified and costUsd fields they return. If the page errors, check the weekly figures call in the analytics module.
